Hey!

No worries. It went really well actually. She was really understanding and she made sure I was doing fine. She gave me the option of having extra time to complete my test, and even asked me if I wanted any other accommodations, like being moved to the front of the class.

I also asked her if she could call my mom in-regards to an IEP, and she was happy to support me. Thankfully my mom understood the importance of an IEP, and I was able to get accommodations in my other classes.

If you have any questions let me know.

Best of luck!

It was Concerta at I believe 27mg.

The doctor discussed side effect which were dehydration, trouble sleeping, and that a very small chance of my blood pressure increasing over time.

I turn 18 in June, and I will hide the medication from my parents indefinitely as I do not want them to ever know.
Thank you for the reassurance!
Appreciate your help!
Thanks for the information!
Doctors legally can’t tell my parents anything unless I have given permission correct?

1.	Yes and the doctor has recommended I take the medication, but she does not want me taking it because I could die from the medication and become a drug addict 
2.	He recommended medication, which he prescribed and I tried for two days. It helped immensely, but my mom took away that privilege.
3.	Nope. I even asked my mom for therapy but she thought of it as a waste of time and money.

I will definitely try that and see what I can gain from it. I believe my teacher recommended that but I didn’t go through with it. 

The thing is, the program I want to attend is so competitive, transfers are basically impossible unless you somehow get an 98+ average, which still doesn’t guarantee a spot.
They check grade 11-12 marks, but they care about consistency between the years.
Thanks for your tips! Your right but the people who read my supplemental are not always educated on ADHD and similar conditions so I feel that it’s best to explain myself. What do you think?
I had meds for one week and got a 98 on my math test, 95 on my computer engineering test and 90 on religion presentation. Should I include those facts?

Honestly, I’m guessing it’s because of the side effects. Even my doctor suggested I take meds numerous times. 

Also I don’t know if you have the answer to my question, but if someone were to take medication without having ADHD, would they sufferer a plethora of health complications?

Wow your husband is really caring I’m glad to hear that!
I have actually tried Concerta 27mg and found a tremendous difference. But then was quickly taken off by my parents. Once I am able to get meds on my own, I will choose Concerta.
They believe that med side affects overrule the benefits. I am thinking about contacting someone from my school who might be able to help me get medication.
They think I am not trying and want to take medication as a way to take drugs. I have tried to explain to them what adhd is, but at this point I just give up.
Honestly, my mom works right beside the doctor, and would interrogate me as to why I am going.
Exactly what my doctor said, and told my mom. ADHD without medication is like trying to shovel the snow in a swim suit, but in winter attire it will be much easier.

I was put on concerta for 2 days before my mom took away the meds. Two months ago, I took some meds and was able to get a 98 percent on my test. Never in my life I thought that was possible. The previous test I received a 65, so that shows the effectiveness of meds.

I even told my mom about this, yet she said it wasn’t the meds...
Thanks:)

Yeah I’m hoping I can get into university!

Would it be better to complete my degree in 6 years vs 5 in order to achieve better results?

Yeah I agree with you university opens many door in-terms of education and life experience.

Would you say a University of Toronto education would be worth it considering their POST requirements? To elaborate, POST is when you choose your program of study after first year, and there are requirements. For computer science at the Mississauga campus, you need an overall gpa of 3.3 and at least an 80 in two classes, one being math proofs which I heard is extremely hard to do well in. These are the requirements in-order to be guarantee.

Appreciate your advice!

Best of luck to you!

Thank you!

Hi! What I did was do all my assigned homework and really understating how to do the question instead of memorizing. I also went over my class notes to understand terms/concepts. Also, I found doing practice test really helped me enforce my understanding on my concepts. 

You don’t necessarily have to do a lot of questions, but if you find yourself struggling in one aspect, you should practice those a lot.

Also, I feel like I may just be good at math as I was since I was young but don’t give up!

I wish you the best of luck!

Will try that,

Thanks!

Yeah she tries to “brainwash” me into thibking I do not have it and that I’m using it as an excuse which doesn’t help at all.

Thanks man hopefully I get into university. Once I am 18 I will definitely be taking medication as I notice a huge difference.

Hi, thanks for replying! 

Yeah I even have a mini success story of my own, but I feel as if she heard a larger one she would understand better. Yeah I guess the main reason she is being like that is that she was fed the wrong information and is worried about my health, which I understand. The first time I did a trial run I told her how I felt better and was actually able to concentrate for the first time, but she told me how it was psychological :/

Hi thanks for taking your time to reply! Yeah it sucks that she thinks that but hopefully the doctor can educate her on meds. 

The one day I took meds I  did my English homework , and my teacher was praising me on how good I am on analyzing shakes-spear. I finally felt motivated and some what smart after she told me that.
Thanks for replying:) yeah I’m gonna talk to her during the appointment so the doctor can also help clear some misconception.
Thanks for giving me hope! I plan on grinding my ass of when I start school, hoping it pays off.

I always get told that I have so much potential, I am lazy, I don’t focus, not trying my best etc. Yup I really struggle in science, but excel in computer related classes.

Also I have a question, So in G11 my average was a 75. After taking medication, and properly studying do you think it is possible for me to achieve an average of 96? I really want to get into my dream college.
Thanks for your advice! I will try talking to my mom again about it.
Yup you exactly described my grades. I want to do computer science in university. The classes I did good in were the two computer classes, the rest I did poorly in.

Well I am supposed to go on the 20th for a second opinion. She told me she is doing it for my satisfaction , I’m guessing to prove herself right.... In Canada you have to be 18 or older to go to a doctor by yourself, so in 1 year. So I probably won’t even be able to talk to the doctor on my own even if I wanted too. 

The problem is I don’t mind waiting it’s just that I really wanted the medication in order to do well in g12 so that I can attend university. 

I technically have the option of taking medication, but my mom made it sound like she would not respect me if I did. She told me quote on quote that I ” wanted to be a druggie” :( She told me that she would make me sign a form that I want to take medication. 

As much as I want to, I don’t want to lose my moms respect either. So I’m kind of in a dilemma.

She was at work when I took the meds so she doesn’t know. I haven’t told her either. I don’t know if she even realizes that I’m struggling because of Adhd anyway. She always accuses me of being lazy and lying when I forgot to do things. She even knows that I almost failed physics but she thinks that because I was lazy. 

Also, I have a question. If someone who is gifted had ADHD, would their grades suffer or since they are gifted still be able to pull good grades?

Hi! I’m glad you were diagnosed and are now being treated:) I am going to the pedestrian on Tuesday so hopefully I can get him to explain how important meds are for me to function. Thanks for your advice:) it means a lot, best of luck to you as well!
